candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, coordinate transitions of care, and assess the need for referrals and resources.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — infectious-diseases review and discharge coordination for OPAT
candidate.educational_objective: Before a client begins OPAT, coordinate infectious-diseases expert review so the indication, antimicrobial choice, route, and outpatient plan are reassessed rather than assuming inpatient IV therapy should automatically continue after discharge.

options.A: Ensure infectious-diseases expert review occurs before OPAT is initiated.
options.B: Arrange OPAT without specialist review because the route of therapy alone determines whether outpatient treatment is appropriate.
options.C: Assume IV therapy must continue if it was started in the hospital, even when expert review identifies an effective oral alternative.
options.D: Delay all discharge planning until the entire antimicrobial course is completed in the hospital.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The current IDSA OPAT guideline recommends infectious-diseases expert review before initiation of OPAT. The rationale includes antimicrobial stewardship: expert review can identify cases in which parenteral therapy is unnecessary, an oral regimen is appropriate, or antimicrobial therapy itself should be modified. B bypasses the recommended review. C incorrectly treats the inpatient IV route as fixed rather than reassessing whether OPAT is needed. D is incorrect because OPAT is specifically a model for completing appropriate parenteral therapy outside the hospital in selected patients.
candidate.source_claim_supported: IDSA recommends infectious-diseases expert review before OPAT is initiated, in part to reassess whether parenteral therapy, the selected antimicrobial, and the outpatient plan are appropriate.
candidate.source_document_title: IDSA 2018 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Outpatient Parenteral Antimicrobial Therapy
candidate.source_locator: Antimicrobial Stewardship, Question XVII, Recommendation 17: all patients should have infectious-diseases expert review prior to initiation of OPAT (strong recommendation, very low-quality evidence). Rationale: expert review can curtail unnecessary OPAT and may identify patients for whom oral or no antimicrobial therapy is appropriate; ID review may occur through traditional consultation, an ID care-transition/OPAT stewardship team, or a collaborative pharmacist/ID-physician model.
candidate.source_version_date: Published November 13, 2018; current IDSA OPAT guideline page reviewed 2026-08-17 with no newer replacement guideline identified
candidate.stem: A hospitalized client is being considered for discharge on outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT). Which care-coordination action is supported by current IDSA OPAT guidance?
